In the fall of 2025, I interned for Sports Info Solutions as a Football Data Scout.  SIS is a sports analytics company that partners with "sportsbooks, odds providers, media companies, fans, leagues and their teams to help them win."  As part of the internship, I had the opportunity to learn how to formally scout players.  Scout School, as it was called, consisted of Zoom meetings centered around a different position each week.  As students during Scout School, we were first taught what to look for in a player, based not only on stats and measurables but also what they put on tape.  We'd then spend time watching film on one specific player, analyzing what he does well and where he needs to improve.

After each class, we'd receive a scouting assignment for the week, which totaled about ten assignments by the end of the internship.  I took on a few additional assignments afterwards to bring my total to fourteen reports.  Based on the likelihood of the player getting drafted, many of these reports could be featured on SIS' NFL Draft Site that will be published in early February.  Others may not be, either because the player has decided not to enter the draft or because he's expected to go undrafted.  Either way, every scouting report is helpful as NFL teams due their due diligence before the Draft in April. So without further ado, here are the links to my scouting reports.
